name: Bellefoungou
details: The Bellefoungou flux tower (latitude 9.791°N, longitude 1.718°E, 445 m asl) consists in an open stand of trees with crown heights of around 15 m, covering 60%–80% of the total soil area. The canopy casts little shade and an annual herbaceous layer, composed of perennial C4 vegetation which varies from 0 (dry season) to 50 cm (wet season) covers the ground. name: Dangbo 1
desc: A mixed crop site, an urban area
details: The flux tower at Dangbo is located in a young (~5 years old) palm oil plantation (latitude 6.607˚N, longitude 2.543˚E), in a tropical humid region within the Ouémé Valley, the second most fertile valley in the world after the Nile. name: Nalohou
details: The flux tower at the Nalohou site (lat. 9.74◦ N, long. 1.60◦ E, 449 m a.s.l) was established in September 2007. It is located in a cultivated area which consists of crops alternating with fallows. The site has been installed in an herbaceous fallow parcel, surrounded by small fields (< 1 ha) with a large variety of rain-fed annual crops (cassava, yam, maize, and groundnut, beans). name: Tambarga
details: As part of a scientific partnership between the École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL, Switzerland) and the Institut International d'Ingénierie de l'Eau et de l'Environnement (2iE, Burkina Faso), a study site was set up in the village of Tambarga, in southeastern Burkina Faso. name: Cocoa-For-Flux
details: Cocoa-For-Flux is an eddy covariance site located in a smallholder cocoa agroforestry plantation in Ntui, central Cameroon (N 4.445666°; E 11.628769°). Instruments are installed at the top of a 55m high mast with shade tree canopies reaching a maximum height of 45m. Shade tree cover is dense (over 40% cover) and diversified (more than 20 species). name: Bia Tano Forest Reserve : GhanaFlux
details: GhanaFLUX is a tropical forest carbon monitoring station located at (7°02'00.0 N, 2°37'21.2 W) within the Bia Tano Forest Reserve, Ghana. name: Agoufou
details: The grassland (Agoufou) grows over bright sandy soil, dominated by annual grasses and forbs with 2% tree cover, mostly scattered Acacia, Combretum, Balanites and Leptadenia.

name: Faidherbia-Flux
details: "Faidherbia-Flux" is a collaborative (> 20 international institutes; > 70 researchers and students) observatory located on a typical agro-silvo-pastoral parkland (groundnut basin, Senegal) dominated by the emblematic and multi-purpose tree species Faidherbia albida, in typical bush-fields cultivated with an annual rotation of pearl millet and groundnut and including the livestock. name: Sob
details: In Senegal, in addition to the instrumented site at Niahkar, near the village of Sob, we have installed a flux tower to monitor the plant dynamics of food crops, known as "home gardens". This observation will enable us to characterize the impact of enriching the soil with manure in comparison with millet crops.
